The classical dn Fourier symbol has full range [theta4(sqrt q)^2,theta3(sqrt q)^2] and long translated plane waves give that essential interval. Trace-class perturbation transfers the essential interval to G; the Schur bounds exclude all outliers. This establishes full equality and exact Riesz constants. All quantifiers and endpoints are explicit; finite checker confirms algebra but does not replace proof.

originality.rationale: Focused published-finding corpus searches and primary full-text comparison found no prior implication of the exact global spectral interval for geometric radial Szegő-kernel Gram chains. The key nonstandard ingredient is the normalized positive correlation-Schur factorization which forbids isolated spectrum despite compact-boundary defects. Primary Baranov–Batenev concerns representing systems, and Pushnitski concerns different integer-index homogeneous Hardy matrices and explicitly allows outliers. Classical Toeplitz and Jacobi identities are acknowledged as established. Residual risk: older interpolating-sequence work may express equivalent sharp bounds under different notation.

value.rationale: The canonical exponentially separated radial interpolation chain gets globally sharp Riesz bounds and its complete spectrum, uniformly in the starting depth. General compact perturbation alone would leave possible outlier eigenvalues, a genuine obstacle resolved by an explicit normalized correlation factor. Theta endpoints give precise coefficient conditioning; the Schur and trace-class identities are reusable structural tools. This is more than a routine finite numerical calculation.
